explanation.text: A 2025 Oregon publication measured Mount Hood at 11,249 feet above sea level. Evidence 4df58c35-46d1-4651-9cee-7078c2b6e901 confirms a 2025 USGS OnDemand Topo page for Mount Hood in Oregon with elevation label 11,249 ft, establishing the publication year and value. Evidence 9e97e006-4157-4c27-9283-2

The assertion that a 2025 Oregon publication measured Mount Hood at 11,249 feet is contradicted by a 1993 Seattle Times article (evidence 66be439c-0c91-4a29-8299-a7624941b84c) reporting 11,240 feet as the measured elevation. The claim's timeframe and measurement value are not supported by that 1993.

Wikipedia (evidence 4978b5e2-ede6-4521-b75d-a5dfd39a2863) states Mount Hood's summit elevation is 11,249 ft NAVD 88 but does not state a 2025 publication date, and other sources cite different measurement years (1991 NGVD, 1993 survey, 1916 Coast and Geodetic Survey).

limitations: The follow-up round limit was reached.

**Mount Hood** is an active [stratovolcano](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stratovolcano "Stratovolcano") in the [Cascade Range](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cascade_Range "Cascade Range") and is a member of the [Cascade Volcanic Arc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cascade_Volcanic_Arc "Cascade Volcanic Arc"). It was formed by a [subduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subduction "Subduction") zone on the [Pacific Coast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Coast_of_the_United_States "West Coast of the United States") and rests in the [Pacific Northwest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Northwest "Pacific Northwest") region of the United States. It is located about 50 miles (80 km) east-east-southeast of [Portland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portland,_Oregon "Portland, Oregon"), on the border between [Clackamas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clackamas_County,_Oregon "Clackamas County, Oregon") and [Hood River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hood_River_County,_Oregon "Hood River County, Oregon") counties, and forms part of the [Mount Hood National Forest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Hood_National_Forest "Mount Hood National Forest"). With a summit elevation of 11,249 feet (3,429 m),[[1]](#cite_note-ngs-1) it is the highest mountain in the U.S. state of [Oregon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oregon "Oregon") and is the fourth highest in the [Cascade Range](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cascade_Range "Cascade Range").[[6]](#cite_note-Swanson-6)
